description: Anthropic / Claude product names as auto-captions and ASR mishear them. Authored for core/quality.py from observed caption errors; deliberately independent of the evaluator's glossary (eval/glossary_default.json), which grades this pass and must not be copied into it. Every rule names an explicit wrong form plus a product context. A bare 'cloud' is never rewritten: 'cloud provider', 'cloud computing', 'AWS cloud', 'in the cloud' are real usage.
syntax: match: case-insensitive regex; {_} = a word gap that may cross a caption-line break and may contain fillers (uh/um). Word boundaries are added automatically. not_before / not_after / require_after are regexes tested against the text immediately before (anchored at its end) or after (anchored at its start) the match. replace: canonical text; when it has as many words as the match (fillers excluded) each word is swapped in place, so a phrase split across lines stays split across the same lines.

rules.name: claude-auth-cli
rules.note: `claude auth status` heard as 'clawed off status'. Only fires before a CLI verb, so the idiom 'clawed off' is untouched.

rules.name: claude-code
rules.note: 'Google Cloud Code' is a real Google product and is left alone.

rules.name: claude-desktop
rules.note: 'virtual cloud desktop' / 'Azure cloud desktop' are real usage.

rules.name: claude-split-word
rules.note: 'Claude' split into two cues: 'claw de decomposes'.

rules.name: clawed-standalone
rules.note: Only in a Claude-domain run (this glossary is selected by metadata). Verb usage — 'clawed back', 'clawed its way', 'the cat clawed the sofa' — is excluded by the neighbour tests.
